report.summary: The only change swaps an observable-state wait (waitFor on session.prompt requests, 5 s bounded poll) for a fixed 200 ms sleep in the `active` helper. That breaks the repo's test rules (CLAUDE.md, docs/CI.md item 4) and makes every run test that uses `active` flaky on busy runners: if the prompt hasn't arrived within 200 ms, requestsOf(...)[index] is undefined and decodeUnknownSync throws. It also adds at least 200 ms to every call. Restore the waitFor line.

findings.text: A fixed sleep replaces waiting for the observable session.prompt request. The test becomes timing-dependent and slower, against CLAUDE.md ('Wait for observable state instead of sleeping') and docs/CI.md item 4 ('Avoid fixed sleeps except when elapsed time is the behavior under test').

evidence.why: Nothing guarantees the Durable Object sends session.prompt within 200 ms. On a busy CI runner, `w.tempod.requestsOf("session.prompt")[index]` is still undefined after the sleep, so `Schema.decodeUnknownSync(...)` throws a parse error and the test fails for reasons unrelated to the behaviour it checks. The previous `waitFor(() => w.tempod.requestsOf("session.prompt").length > index)` checked every 5 ms for up to 5 s. The sleep also adds at least 200 ms to every call even when the prompt arrives in milliseconds, which eats into the 300 s CI check budget. Elapsed time is not the behaviour under test, so the exception in docs/CI.md does not apply.

checked.risk: Tests: sleeps or timing assertions instead of waiting for observable state; budgets too small for loaded runners
Real contracts, failure paths, idempotency, security, build environment, spec: the change is test-only and touches none of these; no spec tab is affected
